summary: Rationale-only status update, validated as no_change with no effects, recording the end state without creating or duplicating records. Both investigations are complete and internally consistent: the configuration-recovery question cites six receipts (single-voter recovery with flag-off controls, the three-voter commit-rule witness, the durable-snapshot corruption surviving a flag-off restart, and the authority pair with both the repeat that lacked its premise and the revised execution that enforces it), and the replay-completion question cites nine receipts (the block, the measured bound, the exact 128-versus-129 delivered-batch boundary, reachability under default settings, and the availability consequence), with every pair reproduced at least twice and identical operands. A final consistency check of 42 claims across 13 retained receipts found no discrepancy; both knowledge corrections raised by this evidence - tuple-counted batching and the randomized snapshot cadence - are recorded with their affected uses marked and their gaps answered. The remaining limitations are structural to the harness (in-memory transports and stores in one process, no production store, no process-level restart or disk fault), which cannot be removed in the remaining allocation without leaving an uncited receipt, so no further work is initiated and the run may expire with this state preserved.
